name: Shakara
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Retired Glottolog entry, merged into Ahwai; only Blench wordlists/survey notes exist, no grammar or phonology located

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2018. Nominal affixes and number marking in the Plateau languages of Central Nigeria. In Watters (ed.), East Benue-Congo: Nouns, pronouns, and verbs, 107-172. Berlin: Language Science Press.
sources.note: Ndunic treated in sec. 2.4 for noun classes only; no prosody.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid pages and bibliographies for shak1238 (1 ref: the ISO CR) and ahwa1235 (7 refs: Blench wordlists 2006/2007, SIL 2015 people-groups survey, ISO CR)
sources.note: No descriptive (grammar/phonology/sketch) reference exists for either languoid.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2007. The Ndun language of Central Nigeria and its affinities (printout 4 Sep 2007); Blench, Roger. 2006. The Nyeng language of Central Nigeria and its affinities (printout 4 Jan 2006). Circulated drafts.
sources.note: Sister lects of the Ahwai cluster; tone only (two tones plus rising/falling), 0 hits for stress/accent.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2014 [Glottolog: 2006]. The Shakara [=Tari] language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft circulated for comment, printout 28 Feb 2014. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. 24 pp. (wordlist paper; data Azhe village 2003)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent (0 hits). Sec. 3 Phonology is 'based on rapid observations.. tentative'; sec. 3.3 Tones, printed p. 3 (p. 5): two tones, most words all low, a few possible glide tones, low unmarked.
sources.venue: The Shakara [=Tari] language of Central Nigeria and its affinities

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. Ndunic page (Ndun / Nyeng / Shakara materials) and any later version of the Shakara wordlist paper.
sources.note: A newer printout could expand the tentative phonology; Blench sometimes adds tone/prosody notes on revision.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Ahwai language' (refs: Ethnologue; Blench Ndunic page; Blench 2018; Blench Ndun/Nyeng/Shakara wordlists; Blench 2012 Akpondu.; Atlas 2019; Blench 2008 Prospecting proto-Plateau)
sources.note: Nothing; names and locations only; cites no phonology.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2008. Prospecting proto-Plateau. Manuscript, Cambridge.
sources.note: Plateau-wide comparative overview; may contain a general remark on Plateau prosody (tone vs stress) applicable to Ndunic, but nothing Shakara-specific expected.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2008. Change Request 2008-017 (Hannelova, Rueck, Yoder, Magnusson, SIL Nigeria Group): merge [nfg] Nyeng and [nfk] Shakara into [nfd], rename Ahwai. 5 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; speakers report the three varieties differ only in 'different intonation' (lay statement); 320-item wordlists, >86% lexical similarity.

sources.citation: Rueck, Michael, Katerina Hannelova, Zachariah Yoder & Carol Magnusson. 2008. A sociolinguistic survey of the Ahwai people, Kaduna State, Nigeria. Jos: SIL Nigeria (unpublished survey report with 320-item comparative wordlists).

sources.access_detail: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: The only other primary data on Shakara/Ahwai; the appended wordlists might be tone-marked, but as a sociolinguistic survey it is unlikely to state a stress rule.

sources.citation: Yashim, David. early 1970s. Orthographic Shakara/Tari wordlist from Ngwan Nungu village (unpublished, 'never checked or re-transcribed', per Blench 2014 p. 1).

sources.note: Only earlier data on the language; orthographic and unchecked, so no prosodic information expected.
